name: What's the difference between standard and noise-reducing sliding doors?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between standard and noise-reducing sliding doors?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in their construction designed for sound insulation. Standard sliding doors typically use single-pane or basic double-pane glass with less emphasis on airtight sealing. Noise-reducing doors, however, utilize specialized laminated or thicker insulated glass units (IGUs) and robust, multi-chambered frames with superior weatherstripping and sealing systems. These advanced features significantly enhance their ability to block and absorb external noise, improving indoor acoustic comfort.
acceptedAnswer.description: Noise-reducing doors use specialized laminated or thicker insulated glass and superior sealing systems, unlike standard doors, to block external sound.
